on_unmapped_default: resolve via viz-kind.json then custom-visual.json (regex) then the generic slicer/filter heuristic; a still-unresolved token is recorded role_class=unsupported with guidance and NEVER coerced to a chart. The historical `VISUAL_KIND.get(vt,'bar')` silent default is GONE.
description: Power BI visual -> Sigma workbook element kind + ROLE CLASS. `source` is the coarse kind token the builder consumes (rec['sigma_kind']); `sigma` is the Sigma element kind; `pbi_visual_types` enumerates the raw PBI visualTypes feeding that token; `role_class` (control|kpi|chart|table|text|image|decoration|unsupported) says what the visual DOES, so the coverage gate can tell a functional loss (a lost slicer = the page lost its filter) from a cosmetic one (a lost decorative shape) from a DIFFERENT cosmetic one that still builds a real element when it can (a logo/banner `image`, which — unlike `decoration` — is never routed to a bare 'nothing built' skip; PbiVizKind.functional? still treats it as non-functional). Both the Ruby builder AND the Python extractors resolve through this one file via lib/pbi_viz_kind.{rb,py} — the previously-duplicated Python VISUAL_KIND dict is gone, so the two maps can no longer drift. Third-party/custom visuals live in custom-visual.json.

sigma_verified.method: LIVE demo-warehouse run (fresh DM): workbook POST clean, 0 type=error, render verified (KPI 127,513.88 = warehouse; column->vertical + bar->horizontal orientation correct)

rows.notes: PBI card / multiRowCard / kpi / gauge -> Sigma kpi-chart. gauge and kpiMatrix have no native Sigma kind (approximated -> approximate_types below); card/multiRowCard/kpi/cardVisual ARE native (approximate:false). A multiRowCard fans out to one kpi-chart per measure in the builder. `cardVisual` is the MODERN card visual type (PBI 2023+); it was absent from the old map and silently became a bar-chart on real customer files.

sigma_verified.method: LIVE demo-warehouse run (fresh DM): workbook POST clean, 0 type=error, render verified (KPI 127,513.88 = warehouse; column->vertical + bar->horizontal orientation correct)

rows.notes: *Bar* families render horizontal (orientation:horizontal), *Column* families vertical (omit orientation). Stacking none|stacked|normalized from the type name. hundredPercentStackedBarChart is now mapped explicitly (it previously fell through the Python `VISUAL_KIND.get(vt,'bar')` default). waterfall/funnel/treemap/ribbon/histogram are DATA-PRESERVING bar approximations -> approximate:true, so they are reported as approximated, not as losses.
Defaults to a SINGLE series unless a Series/Legend role is bound (bead c07).
Line + column combo; the line measure(s) go on Sigma's secondary yAxis2.
PBI matrix/tableEx show a bold Grand Total row by default -> Sigma pivot totals block.
Boxes >= ~60px tall render as an H2 heading; smaller boxes as plain body text.
PBI slicer -> Sigma control. list vs date-range is decided in code (tmsl_date_column?); see control.json.
Resolved to a Sigma region-map or point-map by resolve_map_kind using the model.bim geo dataCategory.

Set directly by extract-report-classic.py for an imageUrl resource (extract-pbir.py has no 'image' visualType). Sigma images are URL-only: needs --image-map {resource: hostedUrl} or the element is skipped with a note. role_class is its OWN 'image', distinct from 'decoration': an image DOES build a real Sigma element (given --image-map) and has its own dedicated coverage entry when it can't (severity:dropped, recoverable — 'Supply --image-map'), unlike a shape/blank which never builds anything and is genuinely cosmetic. Reusing 'decoration' here made every image visual return nil before ever reaching its own build/coverage logic — a regression caught in review.

sigma_verified.method: decorative-only: no data binding, nothing to verify

rows.guidance: Decorative shape/blank with no data binding. Sigma has no shape element; SKIP it. This is a cosmetic difference, NOT a data loss, so it must not count against field coverage. If the shape carried a label, the text is preserved by the adjacent textbox.
rows.notes: Previously coerced to a bar-chart, producing phantom empty charts (5 measured across 2 customer files).

rows.guidance: No Sigma equivalent that preserves the visual's SEMANTICS. Do NOT approximate as a chart — record it as unsupported with the source fields listed so the user can decide. Closest options: decomposition tree / key influencers -> a Sigma pivot table plus a bar chart per driver (the AI ranking itself has no equivalent); Q&A / smart narrative -> a Sigma AI CallText element; python/R visual -> port the script to a Sigma custom plugin or precompute in the warehouse; scorecard/goals -> a KPI element with a reference mark for the target; sankey / word cloud -> a Sigma plugin; play axis -> a Sigma control (animation is not supported).
rows.notes: These previously became bar charts. A bar chart of a decomposition tree is not an approximation, it is a wrong answer — hence role_class unsupported, reported honestly.
